units.source_text: 我曾就一片草叶尖端的锐角进行过长时间的思考。

en.t: I once spent a long time thinking about the sharp angle at the tip of a blade of grass.
To call it thinking is not quite right.

units.source_text: 这种奇怪的琐碎的念头决不会持久，

en.t: This strange and trivial notion would never last for long,

units.source_text: 在我的感觉里，它做活着，又似死去，实在难以捕捉，

en.t: and in my feeling it seemed alive and yet also dead, truly hard to grasp,

units.source_text: 犹如乐曲的副歌执拗地反复出现。

en.t: like the refrain of a piece of music stubbornly appearing again and again.

units.source_text: 这片草叶的尖端为什么其锐角必须是这样尖锐的呢？

en.t: Why did the sharp angle at the tip of this blade of grass have to be so sharp?
If it were an obtuse angle,

units.source_text: 难道就会失去草的种别，就得自然从这一角整个崩溃吗？

en.t: would it lose its identity as grass, and would nature itself have to collapse entirely from that one angle?

units.source_text: 倘使是拆掉大自然的齿轮中的极小东西，

en.t: If one were to remove some tiny thing from the gears of great nature,

units.source_text: 不就可以使整个大自然颠覆吗？

en.t: could that not overturn the whole of nature?

units.source_text: 我想人非非，陡然地思考着这种方法。

en.t: My thoughts ran into wild fancies, and all at once I was thinking about such a method.
